note: Formula sheet for the daily 5-minute speed round (pedagogy-spec §2 Tier 1) and for the Numericals Engine to quote a formula line by line. `unit` values are the canonical CDC unit names used by js/grow.js, so a sheet can be auto-assembled from the units he has covered. `formulaHTML` is deliberately PLAIN TEXT with unicode subscripts and superscripts — it carries no markup and must be rendered with el({text}) or the .formula component class, never through innerHTML. `commonTrap` is the documented mark-loser for that formula and is what the speed round should surface after a miss; several map onto the misconception ids in pedagogy-spec §3.6.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Least count of a vernier calliper
formulas.formulaHTML: LC = (value of 1 main-scale division) / (number of vernier divisions)
formulas.symbols: LC in cm or mm
formulas.conditions: Any vernier calliper. With a millimetre main scale and 10 vernier divisions, LC = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm.
formulas.commonTrap: Quoting 0.1 cm instead of 0.01 cm. Write the unit on the least count itself, then every reading inherits it.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Least count of a screw gauge
formulas.formulaHTML: LC = pitch / (number of circular-scale divisions)
formulas.symbols: pitch = distance the spindle advances in one full rotation
formulas.conditions: Any micrometer screw gauge. Pitch 1 mm with 100 divisions gives LC = 0.01 mm.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the number of main-scale divisions instead of circular-scale divisions.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Reading an instrument with a zero error
formulas.formulaHTML: corrected reading = MSR + (coinciding division × LC) − zero error
formulas.symbols: MSR = main-scale reading
formulas.conditions: Vernier callipers and screw gauges alike; the zero error is read with the jaws fully closed.
formulas.commonTrap: Adding a negative zero error instead of subtracting it. Subtract the zero error with its own sign, always.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Mean value and mean absolute error
formulas.formulaHTML: ā = (a₁ + a₂ + … + aₙ) / n  ·  Δā = (|Δa₁| + |Δa₂| + … + |Δaₙ|) / n
formulas.symbols: aᵢ = individual readings, Δaᵢ = aᵢ − ā
formulas.conditions: Repeated readings of one quantity with the same instrument.
formulas.commonTrap: Letting the signed errors cancel. Take the modulus of every deviation before averaging.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Relative and percentage error
formulas.formulaHTML: relative error = Δā / ā  ·  percentage error = (Δā / ā) × 100%
formulas.symbols: Δā = mean absolute error
formulas.conditions: Reporting the reliability of any measured quantity.
formulas.commonTrap: Reporting a percentage error to more figures than the measurement itself justifies.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Error in a product, quotient or power
formulas.formulaHTML: Δz / z = p(Δa / a) + q(Δb / b) + r(Δc / c), where p, q, r are the powers of a, b, c in z
formulas.symbols: p, q, r are the powers; errors always ADD
formulas.conditions: Combining measured quantities. For a sphere V depends on r³, so the percentage error in V is 3 × the percentage error in r.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting that a power multiplies the fractional error, and that errors add even when the quantities divide.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Significant-figure rules
formulas.formulaHTML: multiply or divide → keep the fewest significant figures  ·  add or subtract → keep the fewest decimal places
formulas.conditions: Every calculated answer in physics and chemistry. Round once, at the very end.
formulas.commonTrap: Rounding at every intermediate step, and copying the calculator display in full. Both lose marks under PH-U05.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Converting a quantity between systems of units
formulas.formulaHTML: n₁u₁ = n₂u₂  ⇒  n₂ = n₁ (M₁ / M₂)ᵃ (L₁ / L₂)ᵇ (T₁ / T₂)ᶜ
formulas.symbols: a, b, c are the powers of M, L, T in the dimensional formula
formulas.conditions: Converting between SI and CGS, for example 1 N = 1 × 10⁵ dyne, 1 J = 1 × 10⁷ erg.
formulas.commonTrap: Inverting a ratio. The bigger unit always carries the smaller number, so check the direction against a case you know.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Principle of homogeneity of dimensions
formulas.formulaHTML: every term on both sides of a correct equation has the same dimensions
formulas.conditions: Checking any derived equation before you trust it, and deriving a relation when the dependence is known.
formulas.commonTrap: Treating a dimensionally correct equation as proved. The method is blind to dimensionless factors such as ½ and 2π.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Dimensional formulae worth knowing cold
formulas.formulaHTML: force MLT⁻² · work, energy, torque ML²T⁻² · power ML²T⁻³ · pressure, stress ML⁻¹T⁻² · momentum, impulse MLT⁻¹ · frequency T⁻¹ · G M⁻¹L³T⁻² · h ML²T⁻¹ · viscosity ML⁻¹T⁻¹ · surface tension MT⁻²
formulas.conditions: Any dimensional check, conversion or derivation in the paper.
formulas.commonTrap: Assuming that two quantities with the same dimensions are the same quantity — work and torque share ML²T⁻² and are not interchangeable.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Resultant of two vectors (parallelogram law)
formulas.formulaHTML: R = √(P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ)  ·  tan α = Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ)
formulas.symbols: θ = angle between P and Q, α = angle of R with P
formulas.conditions: Two coplanar vectors acting at a point.
formulas.commonTrap: Adding magnitudes arithmetically. At right angles 3 N and 4 N give 5 N, never 7 N.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Resolution of a vector
formulas.formulaHTML: Fx = F cos θ  ·  Fy = F sin θ  ·  F = √(Fx² + Fy²)
formulas.symbols: θ measured from the x-axis
formulas.conditions: Inclined planes, projectiles, forces in equilibrium.
formulas.commonTrap: Swapping sine and cosine. Tie each one to its angle on the diagram before substituting.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion
formulas.formulaHTML: v = u + at  ·  s = ut + ½at²  ·  v² = u² + 2as  ·  sₙ = u + a(2n − 1) / 2
formulas.symbols: u, v in m s⁻¹, a in m s⁻², s in m, t in s
formulas.conditions: Constant acceleration in a straight line only.
formulas.commonTrap: Assuming u = 0 when the body is already moving (PH-U04), and mixing signs of a and s for a body thrown upwards.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Projectile fired at an angle
formulas.formulaHTML: T = 2u sin θ / g  ·  H = u² sin²θ / 2g  ·  R = u² sin 2θ / g
formulas.symbols: T = time of flight, H = maximum height, R = horizontal range
formulas.conditions: Projection from and landing on the same horizontal level, air resistance neglected.
formulas.commonTrap: Using sin θ where sin 2θ belongs in the range. Maximum range is at θ = 45°.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Newton's second law and impulse
formulas.formulaHTML: F = ma = dp/dt  ·  impulse = FΔt = Δp = mv − mu
formulas.symbols: p = mv, the linear momentum
formulas.conditions: Constant mass. For variable mass use the rate of change of momentum form.
formulas.commonTrap: Dropping the sign of the change in momentum for a rebound: a ball reversing direction has Δp = m(v − (−u)).

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Friction and the angle of friction
formulas.formulaHTML: f = μN  ·  tan λ = μ  ·  on an incline N = mg cos θ
formulas.symbols: μ = coefficient of friction, λ = angle of friction
formulas.conditions: Limiting friction; static and kinetic coefficients differ.
formulas.commonTrap: Using N = mg on an inclined plane. On an incline the normal reaction is mg cos θ.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Work, energy and the work–energy theorem
formulas.formulaHTML: W = Fs cos θ  ·  KE = ½mv²  ·  PE = mgh  ·  net work = ΔKE
formulas.symbols: θ = angle between force and displacement
formulas.conditions: W = Fs cos θ needs a constant force; otherwise take the area under the force–displacement graph.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting cos θ, and quoting energy in newtons. Energy is in joules on every line.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Power
formulas.formulaHTML: P = W / t = Fv  ·  efficiency = (useful output / total input) × 100%
formulas.symbols: P in watts, 1 hp = 746 W
formulas.conditions: P = Fv gives the instantaneous power when F and v are along the same line.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving efficiency out of a machine or hydro-power numerical — it is usually one of the marks.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Centripetal acceleration and force
formulas.formulaHTML: a = v² / r = ω²r  ·  F = mv² / r = mω²r  ·  v = rω
formulas.symbols: ω in rad s⁻¹, ω = 2π / T
formulas.conditions: Uniform circular motion; the force points to the centre.
formulas.commonTrap: Inventing an outward centrifugal force in an inertial frame (PH-F11). Nothing pushes the body outwards.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Banking of a road and the conical pendulum
formulas.formulaHTML: tan θ = v² / rg  ·  conical pendulum: T = 2π √(l cos θ / g)
formulas.symbols: θ = angle of banking, l = string length
formulas.conditions: Frictionless banking for the design speed.
formulas.commonTrap: Putting g on the wrong side. Check by dimensions: v² / rg must be a pure number.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Newton's law of gravitation and g
formulas.formulaHTML: F = G m₁m₂ / r²  ·  g = GM / R²
formulas.symbols: G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², M and R are the mass and radius of the Earth
formulas.conditions: Point masses, or uniform spheres with r measured centre to centre.
formulas.commonTrap: Measuring r from the surface instead of the centre of the Earth.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Variation of g with height and depth
formulas.formulaHTML: height: g_h = g(1 − 2h / R)  for h ≪ R  ·  depth: g_d = g(1 − d / R)
formulas.symbols: h = height above the surface, d = depth below it
formulas.conditions: The height formula is the approximation for h ≪ R; the exact form is g_h = gR² / (R + h)².
formulas.commonTrap: Using the h ≪ R approximation for a satellite. At satellite heights you need the exact form.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Orbital velocity and escape velocity
formulas.formulaHTML: v₀ = √(GM / r) = √(gR² / r)  ·  vₑ = √(2GM / R) = √(2gR) = 11.2 km s⁻¹
formulas.symbols: r = radius of orbit from the centre of the Earth
formulas.conditions: Circular orbit; escape velocity is independent of the mass of the escaping body.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting vₑ = √2 × v₀ at the surface, and quoting 11.2 m s⁻¹ instead of 11.2 km s⁻¹.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Period of a satellite and Kepler's third law
formulas.formulaHTML: T = 2π √(r³ / GM)  ·  T² ∝ r³
formulas.symbols: geostationary satellite: T = 24 h, r ≈ 42 400 km
formulas.conditions: Circular orbits about the same central body.
formulas.commonTrap: Comparing periods with radii measured from the surface — Kepler needs the distance from the centre.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Stress, strain and Young's modulus
formulas.formulaHTML: stress = F / A  ·  strain = ΔL / L  ·  Y = stress / strain = FL / (A ΔL)
formulas.symbols: Y in N m⁻², strain has no unit
formulas.conditions: Within the elastic limit, where Hooke's law holds.
formulas.commonTrap: Giving strain a unit. Strain is a ratio of two lengths, so it is dimensionless.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Energy stored in a stretched wire
formulas.formulaHTML: U = ½ F ΔL  ·  energy per unit volume = ½ × stress × strain
formulas.symbols: U in joules
formulas.conditions: Loading within the elastic limit, with the load raised gradually.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting the ½. The force grows from zero to F, so only the average force does work.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Temperature-scale conversion
formulas.symbols: C = °C, F = °F, K = kelvin
formulas.conditions: Any conversion between the three scales.
formulas.commonTrap: Substituting °C where the equation needs kelvin (PH-U02). Gas-law and radiation formulae are always kelvin.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Linear, superficial and cubical expansion
formulas.formulaHTML: L = L₀(1 + αΔθ)  ·  A = A₀(1 + βΔθ)  ·  V = V₀(1 + γΔθ)  ·  β = 2α, γ = 3α
formulas.symbols: α in K⁻¹ or °C⁻¹
formulas.conditions: Isotropic solids and small temperature changes.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the original length where the expanded length belongs, and mixing α with γ for a solid sphere.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Heat gained, heat lost and latent heat
formulas.formulaHTML: Q = mcΔθ  ·  Q = mL  ·  heat lost = heat gained
formulas.symbols: c = specific heat capacity in J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L = specific latent heat in J kg⁻¹
formulas.conditions: No heat exchanged with the surroundings; use Q = mL at a change of state, where the temperature does not change.
formulas.commonTrap: Using Q = mcΔθ across a phase change. Ice melting at 0 °C absorbs mL with Δθ = 0.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Conduction and Stefan's law
formulas.formulaHTML: Q / t = kA(θ₁ − θ₂) / l  ·  E = σT⁴
formulas.symbols: k = thermal conductivity in W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴
formulas.conditions: Steady state, and lagged bars for conduction. Stefan's law needs absolute temperature.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving the thickness in centimetres, and putting °C into T⁴.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Gas laws and the ideal-gas equation
formulas.formulaHTML: p₁V₁ / T₁ = p₂V₂ / T₂  ·  pV = nRT = (m / M)RT
formulas.symbols: R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, T in kelvin always
formulas.conditions: An ideal gas; a fixed mass for the combined gas law.
formulas.commonTrap: Working in °C. Every gas-law temperature is in kelvin (PH-U02).

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Kinetic theory of gases
formulas.formulaHTML: p = ⅓ ρ c̄²  ·  pV = ⅓ mN c̄²  ·  ½ m c̄² = (3/2) kT  ·  c_rms = √(3RT / M)
formulas.symbols: k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, M = molar mass in kg mol⁻¹
formulas.conditions: An ideal gas of point molecules with no intermolecular forces.
formulas.commonTrap: Putting M in g mol⁻¹ into c_rms. Use kg mol⁻¹ with R in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Mirror formula and magnification
formulas.formulaHTML: 1 / f = 1 / v + 1 / u  ·  m = − v / u = height of image / height of object  ·  f = R / 2
formulas.symbols: real-is-positive convention as used in the NEB text
formulas.conditions: Paraxial rays on spherical mirrors.
formulas.commonTrap: Mixing sign conventions midway. Fix the convention at the top of the answer and state it (PH-U03).

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Refraction, real and apparent depth
formulas.formulaHTML: n = sin i / sin r  ·  n = real depth / apparent depth  ·  ₁n₂ = n₂ / n₁
formulas.symbols: n = refractive index, no unit
formulas.conditions: Light passing between two transparent media; the apparent-depth rule needs near-normal viewing.
formulas.commonTrap: Inverting the refractive index. Light entering a denser medium bends towards the normal — check the ray diagram.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Critical angle and total internal reflection
formulas.formulaHTML: sin C = 1 / n
formulas.symbols: C = critical angle
formulas.conditions: Light travelling from a denser to a rarer medium, at an angle greater than C.
formulas.commonTrap: Applying it in the wrong direction. There is no total internal reflection going from rarer to denser.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Prism formula and minimum deviation
formulas.formulaHTML: A + δ = i + e  ·  n = sin((A + δₘ) / 2) / sin(A / 2)
formulas.symbols: A = angle of prism, δₘ = angle of minimum deviation
formulas.conditions: δₘ needs the symmetric passage, where i = e and the ray inside runs parallel to the base.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the minimum-deviation formula for any deviation. It is only true at minimum deviation.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Lens formula, magnification and power
formulas.formulaHTML: 1 / f = 1 / v − 1 / u  ·  m = v / u  ·  P = 1 / f (f in metres)
formulas.symbols: P in dioptres, D
formulas.conditions: Thin lenses and paraxial rays.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving f in centimetres when calculating power. f = 25 cm gives P = +4 D, not +0.04 D (PH-U01).

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Lens maker's formula and lenses in contact
formulas.symbols: R₁, R₂ = radii of curvature with sign
formulas.conditions: Thin lens in air; the combination formula needs the lenses in contact.
formulas.commonTrap: Ignoring the signs of R₁ and R₂ — they are what make a lens converging or diverging.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Coulomb's law
formulas.formulaHTML: F = (1 / 4πε₀) q₁q₂ / r²  ·  1 / 4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²
formulas.symbols: ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²
formulas.conditions: Point charges at rest, in vacuum; divide by the relative permittivity in a medium.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving r in centimetres. Convert to metres before squaring, or the answer is out by 10⁴.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Electric field and potential of a point charge
formulas.formulaHTML: E = F / q = (1 / 4πε₀) Q / r²  ·  V = (1 / 4πε₀) Q / r  ·  E = − dV / dr
formulas.symbols: E in N C⁻¹ or V m⁻¹, V in volts
formulas.conditions: Point charge in vacuum; potential is a scalar, field is a vector.
formulas.commonTrap: Adding potentials as vectors. Potentials add algebraically with their signs; fields add as vectors.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Capacitance and the parallel-plate capacitor
formulas.formulaHTML: C = Q / V  ·  C = ε₀A / d  ·  with a dielectric C = Kε₀A / d
formulas.symbols: C in farads, K = dielectric constant
formulas.conditions: Uniform field between close parallel plates.
formulas.commonTrap: Assuming the charge stays constant when the battery is left connected — with the battery on, V is fixed and Q changes.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Capacitors in series and parallel, energy stored
formulas.formulaHTML: series: 1 / C = 1 / C₁ + 1 / C₂  ·  parallel: C = C₁ + C₂  ·  U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q² / 2C
formulas.symbols: U in joules
formulas.conditions: Ideal capacitors, no leakage.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the resistor rules. Capacitors add in PARALLEL and take reciprocals in SERIES — the opposite of resistors.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Ohm's law and resistivity
formulas.formulaHTML: V = IR  ·  R = ρl / A  ·  R_t = R₀(1 + αt)
formulas.symbols: ρ = resistivity in Ω m, α = temperature coefficient
formulas.conditions: Ohmic conductors at constant temperature.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting that stretching a wire changes both l and A, so R changes as the square of the stretch factor.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Resistors in series and parallel
formulas.formulaHTML: series: R = R₁ + R₂ + R₃  ·  parallel: 1 / R = 1 / R₁ + 1 / R₂ + 1 / R₃
formulas.symbols: R in ohms
formulas.conditions: Steady direct current.
formulas.commonTrap: Stopping at 1 / R and calling it the answer. Invert at the end to get R.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Kirchhoff's laws
formulas.formulaHTML: junction rule: ΣI = 0  ·  loop rule: ΣE = ΣIR
formulas.symbols: signs follow the chosen loop direction
formulas.conditions: Any network too tangled for series-parallel reduction.
formulas.commonTrap: Changing the sign convention halfway round the loop. Mark the direction on the diagram first and keep it.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Wheatstone bridge and the metre bridge
formulas.formulaHTML: balanced when P / Q = R / S  ·  metre bridge: R / S = l / (100 − l)
formulas.symbols: l = balancing length in cm
formulas.conditions: At balance, when the galvanometer reads zero.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the balance condition when the bridge is not balanced.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: EMF, internal resistance and electrical power
formulas.formulaHTML: E = I(R + r)  ·  V = E − Ir  ·  P = VI = I²R = V² / R
formulas.symbols: r = internal resistance of the cell
formulas.conditions: Steady current from a real cell.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the terminal voltage where the emf belongs. They are equal only when no current flows.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Radioactive decay and half-life
formulas.formulaHTML: N = N₀e^(−λt) → after n half-lives N = N₀ / 2ⁿ  ·  t½ = 0.693 / λ  ·  activity A = λN
formulas.symbols: λ = decay constant in s⁻¹, activity in becquerel
formulas.conditions: A large number of identical nuclei; decay is a statistical law.
formulas.commonTrap: Treating half-life as "half the total life". After two half-lives one quarter remains, never nothing.

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.label: Mass defect and binding energy
formulas.formulaHTML: Δm = [Zm_p + (A − Z)m_n] − M_nucleus  ·  E = Δm c²  ·  1 u = 931.5 MeV
formulas.symbols: A = mass number, Z = atomic number
formulas.conditions: Nuclear reactions and stability comparisons.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving Δm in atomic mass units and multiplying by c² in SI. Use the 931.5 MeV per u shortcut, or convert to kilograms first.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Moles from mass — the bridge formula
formulas.formulaHTML: n = m / M  ·  m = n × M  ·  M = m / n
formulas.symbols: n in mol, m in g, M in g mol⁻¹
formulas.conditions: Any pure substance, solid, liquid or gas.
formulas.commonTrap: Treating the mole as a mass (CH-M01). A mole is a count; the gram is the mass. Write the unit on every line.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Moles to particles
formulas.formulaHTML: N = n × Nₐ  ·  Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
formulas.symbols: N = number of atoms, molecules or ions
formulas.conditions: Always. Multiply by the atoms per formula unit when the question asks for atoms, not molecules.
formulas.commonTrap: Confusing molecules with atoms (CH-M04). 1 mol of CO₂ is 6.022 × 10²³ molecules but 1.807 × 10²⁴ atoms.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Moles to volume at STP
formulas.formulaHTML: n = V / 22.4 (V in litres)  ·  V = n × 22.4 L
formulas.symbols: STP = 273 K and 1 atm
formulas.conditions: GASES only, and only at STP. Use pV = nRT at any other temperature or pressure.
formulas.commonTrap: Applying 22.4 L to a solid, a liquid, or a gas at room temperature (CH-M06).

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: The mole roadmap
formulas.formulaHTML: mass ⇄ moles ⇄ particles  ·  moles ⇄ volume at STP  ·  every route passes through moles
formulas.symbols: ÷M and ×M · ×Nₐ and ÷Nₐ · ×22.4 and ÷22.4
formulas.conditions: Every stoichiometry question. Convert to moles first, use the balanced equation, then convert out.
formulas.commonTrap: Trying to go from grams straight to litres or particles. Nothing crosses without passing through moles.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Molar mass and molecular mass
formulas.formulaHTML: molecular mass (amu) and molar mass (g mol⁻¹) are numerically equal
formulas.symbols: H₂O: 18 amu per molecule, 18 g mol⁻¹ per mole
formulas.conditions: Any compound. The molar mass is the sum of the atomic masses of every atom in the formula.
formulas.commonTrap: Writing g mol⁻¹ where amu belongs, or leaving the unit off entirely (CH-M03).

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Vapour density
formulas.formulaHTML: molar mass = 2 × vapour density  ·  VD = M / 2
formulas.symbols: vapour density has no unit
formulas.conditions: Gases and volatile liquids, compared against hydrogen.
formulas.commonTrap: Reporting vapour density in g mol⁻¹. It is a ratio of two densities, so it has no unit.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Percentage composition by mass
formulas.formulaHTML: % of element = (mass of that element in 1 mol / molar mass) × 100%
formulas.conditions: Any compound of known formula. The percentages must add to 100 — that is the check.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting the subscript. NH₄NO₃ holds 2 nitrogen atoms, so 28 g out of 80 g, which is 35%.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Empirical formula from percentage composition
formulas.formulaHTML: % → grams (take 100 g) → moles (÷ atomic mass) → ÷ smallest → × a whole number if needed
formulas.symbols: result = simplest whole-number ratio
formulas.conditions: Percentage or mass composition data.
formulas.commonTrap: Stopping at a ratio like 1 : 1.5. Multiply the whole set by 2 (or by 3 for .33 and .67), never round it away.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Molecular formula from the empirical formula
formulas.formulaHTML: n = molar mass / empirical formula mass  ·  molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ
formulas.symbols: n is a whole number
formulas.conditions: Needs the molar mass, from vapour density or from the question.
formulas.commonTrap: Rounding n from 1.9 up to 2 without checking the arithmetic — an n that is not close to a whole number means an earlier slip.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Limiting reactant
formulas.formulaHTML: for each reactant compute moles ÷ coefficient  ·  the smallest value is the limiting reactant
formulas.symbols: the limiting reactant fixes every product amount
formulas.conditions: Any reaction where the amounts of two or more reactants are given.
formulas.commonTrap: Choosing the reactant with the smaller MASS (CH-S03). Mass says nothing; only moles ÷ coefficient decides.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Excess reactant left over
formulas.formulaHTML: excess left = (moles taken − moles used) × M  ·  moles used = coefficient ratio × moles of limiting reactant
formulas.conditions: After the limiting reactant has been identified.
formulas.commonTrap: Reporting the leftover in moles when the question asked for grams (CH-S04).

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Theoretical, experimental and percentage yield
formulas.formulaHTML: % yield = (experimental yield / theoretical yield) × 100%
formulas.symbols: theoretical yield comes from the limiting reactant
formulas.conditions: Real reactions, which lose product to side reactions, reversibility and transfer losses.
formulas.commonTrap: Computing the theoretical yield from the reactant in excess (CH-S07). A yield above 100% means a wet or impure product.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: The laws of stoichiometry
formulas.formulaHTML: conservation of mass · definite proportions · multiple proportions · reciprocal proportions
formulas.conditions: Chemical combination by mass; they are what the balanced equation encodes.
formulas.commonTrap: Balancing an equation by changing a subscript (CH-S05). Subscripts define the substance; only coefficients may change.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Avogadro's law
formulas.formulaHTML: equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules
formulas.symbols: so V ∝ n at fixed T and p
formulas.conditions: Gases only. It is what makes the 22.4 L molar volume and the volume ratios in gaseous reactions work.
formulas.commonTrap: Applying volume ratios to reactions with a solid or liquid reactant — the ratio rule is for gases.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Energy of a photon
formulas.formulaHTML: E = hν = hc / λ  ·  h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s  ·  c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
formulas.symbols: ν in Hz, λ in m, E in J
formulas.conditions: Electromagnetic radiation of a single frequency.
formulas.commonTrap: Leaving λ in nanometres. Convert to metres first, or the energy is out by a factor of 10⁹.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Rydberg equation for the hydrogen spectrum
formulas.symbols: n₂ > n₁; Lyman n₁ = 1, Balmer n₁ = 2
formulas.conditions: Hydrogen and hydrogen-like species only.
formulas.commonTrap: Swapping n₁ and n₂ and getting a negative wavelength. The lower level is always n₁.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Bohr energy levels of hydrogen
formulas.formulaHTML: Eₙ = −13.6 / n² eV  ·  rₙ = 0.529 n² Å
formulas.symbols: n = principal quantum number
formulas.conditions: Single-electron species; multiply by Z² for He⁺ and Li²⁺.
formulas.commonTrap: Dropping the minus sign. Bound electron energies are negative; the ionisation energy is the positive difference.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Quantum-number rules
formulas.formulaHTML: l = 0 to (n − 1)  ·  m = −l to +l  ·  s = ±½  ·  maximum electrons in a shell = 2n²
formulas.symbols: orbitals in a subshell = 2l + 1
formulas.conditions: Every electronic configuration and every "is this set possible" question.
formulas.commonTrap: Allowing l = n. For n = 2 the only values are l = 0 and l = 1.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Boyle's law, Charles's law and the combined gas law
formulas.formulaHTML: p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ (T fixed)  ·  V₁ / T₁ = V₂ / T₂ (p fixed)  ·  p₁V₁ / T₁ = p₂V₂ / T₂
formulas.symbols: T in kelvin always
formulas.conditions: A fixed mass of an ideal gas.
formulas.commonTrap: Using °C. Convert with T(K) = t(°C) + 273 before anything else.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Ideal-gas equation
formulas.formulaHTML: pV = nRT = (m / M)RT  ·  density ρ = pM / RT
formulas.symbols: R = 0.0821 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ or 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹
formulas.conditions: An ideal gas; pick the R that matches your pressure and volume units.
formulas.commonTrap: Mixing atmospheres with joules. Match R to the units, then write the unit on every line.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Dalton's law of partial pressures
formulas.formulaHTML: p_total = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ + …  ·  pᵢ = xᵢ × p_total
formulas.symbols: xᵢ = mole fraction of component i
formulas.conditions: Non-reacting gas mixtures. For a gas collected over water, subtract the aqueous tension.
formulas.commonTrap: Forgetting to subtract the aqueous tension when a gas is collected over water.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Graham's law of diffusion
formulas.formulaHTML: r ∝ 1 / √M  ·  r₁ / r₂ = √(M₂ / M₁) = √(d₂ / d₁)
formulas.symbols: r = rate of diffusion or effusion
formulas.conditions: Same temperature and pressure for both gases.
formulas.commonTrap: Inverting the ratio. The lighter gas diffuses FASTER, so its rate goes on top.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Concentration measures
formulas.formulaHTML: molarity M = moles of solute / volume of solution in L  ·  molality m = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg  ·  mole fraction x = n₁ / n_total
formulas.symbols: M in mol L⁻¹, m in mol kg⁻¹
formulas.conditions: Molarity changes with temperature because volume does; molality does not.
formulas.commonTrap: Dividing by the mass of the SOLVENT for molarity, or by the volume of the solution for molality (CH-M07).

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Dilution and titration
formulas.formulaHTML: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂  ·  for a reaction: M₁V₁ / n₁ = M₂V₂ / n₂
formulas.symbols: n₁, n₂ = stoichiometric coefficients
formulas.conditions: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ is for dilution or a 1 : 1 reaction; otherwise divide by the coefficients.
formulas.commonTrap: Using M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ for an acid–base pair that does not react 1 : 1, such as H₂SO₄ with NaOH.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Oxidation-number rules
formulas.formulaHTML: free element 0 · H is +1 (−1 in hydrides) · O is −2 (−1 in peroxides) · sum = 0 in a molecule, = charge in an ion
formulas.conditions: Assigning oxidation numbers and identifying what is oxidised or reduced.
formulas.commonTrap: Confusing oxidation number with valency, and forgetting the sign in a polyatomic ion.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Equivalent weight
formulas.formulaHTML: equivalent weight = molar mass / n-factor  ·  normality N = molarity × n-factor
formulas.symbols: n-factor = electrons gained or lost, or replaceable H⁺ or OH⁻
formulas.conditions: Redox and neutralisation calculations; N₁V₁ = N₂V₂ at the end point.
formulas.commonTrap: Using the same n-factor for a substance in every reaction. The n-factor depends on the reaction it is in.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Equilibrium constant
formulas.formulaHTML: Kc = [products] / [reactants], each raised to its coefficient  ·  Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn
formulas.symbols: Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants
formulas.conditions: A reversible reaction at equilibrium, at a fixed temperature. Pure solids and liquids are left out.
formulas.commonTrap: Including a pure solid or liquid in the expression, and forgetting that only temperature changes K.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.label: Le Chatelier's principle
formulas.formulaHTML: a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose any change imposed on it
formulas.symbols: change: concentration, pressure, temperature
formulas.conditions: Predicting the direction of a shift; industrial conditions for the Haber and Contact processes come from it.
formulas.commonTrap: Saying that a catalyst shifts the equilibrium. A catalyst speeds both directions equally and shifts nothing.
